To start with, I don't believe Reddit is going to be abandoned like digg was. If that happens, then I would love it, but realistically, Reddit will survive for a long time.

BUT, during that time, I see Reddit and Voat having huge fights. Here are my reasons:

  • Voat allows Reddit's subreddits to be mirrored. If Reddit shuts down a subreddit, it will be opened at Voat. But I guess Reddit Biz don't care about that

  • Brigading, which is Reddit's biggest problem, can be be circumvented through voat. In order to curb brigading, Reddit must figure out mechanisms to deal with Voat traffic. There are bots which currently inform you if a thread has been posted elsewhere, those bots will flow in both directions(and only Reddit loses in this situation).

  • Game of Trolls: Most people don't remember the days of Game of Trolls, but I remember those days. /r/GameOfTrolls was such an effective annoyance to the Reddit Admins that it went out with /r/jailbait. A GameOfTrolls subreddit on Voat would create super annoyance for Reddit. Most Voaters think that Reddit's pro-SJW stance would make them lose their loyal audience. According to me, the biggest damage would be dealt through subreddits such as GameOfTrolls with the sheer aim to troll people on Reddit and Reddit Admins not having any ability to curb things.

I'm probably just gonna hide in my niche-topic subverses/subreddits of interest where nothing political ever happens. That's probably the only way I even survived Reddit in the first place.
